headline: Jet fuel peaked at $5.07 a gallon on 2022-04-28; United's matched fare index (100 on 2022-04-17) peaked at 148 on 2022-06-01, 34 days later, and stood at 101 on 2022-10-05. Across 23 weekly changes the summed 4-week response of United fares to a 1% fuel move is +1.30% (95% interval +0.28% to +2.32%); the interval includes zero in 6 of the 12 United specifications tried, and the window spans the summer travel peak.
plain_summary: Gulf Coast jet fuel: $3.85 on 2022-04-18, a high of $5.07 on 2022-04-28 (+32% from the start), a low of $2.94 on 2022-08-08, and $3.64 on 2022-10-05 (-5% from the start). Matched nonstop economy fare index, 100 on 2022-04-17: United high 148 on 2022-06-01, low 88 on 2022-08-16, end 101 (last week against first week -1%); Delta high 119 on 2022-06-01, low 99 on 2022-04-18, end 105 (last week against first week +3%); American high 141 on 2022-05-23, low 98 on 2022-04-18, end 107 (last week against first week +7%); all carriers high 137 on 2022-05-23, low 91 on 2022-08-30, end 99 (last week against first week -2%). Counting basic-economy quotes too (cheapest economy fare of either kind), the United index peaks at 138 on 2022-05-11 and ends at 87; basic economy went from 9% of United's nonstop economy quote rows in 2022-05 to 46% in 2022-09. Weekly changes in the United index against weekly fuel changes at 21 leads and lags (-8 to +12 weeks): same-week correlation +0.15 (95% interval -0.33 to +0.40); largest in size +0.52 at +5 weeks (interval +0.11 to +0.74; a positive lag means fuel moved first). 1 of 21 intervals exclude zero; about one would by chance. United fares, without the TSA traveler control: a 1% rise in fuel goes with a +1.29% change in the fare index summed over the same week and the 4 weeks after (95% interval +0.24% to +2.34%, 23 weeks, 6 parameters); the interval lies above zero. United fares, with the TSA traveler control: a 1% rise in fuel goes with a +1.30% change in the fare index summed over the same week and the 4 weeks after (95% interval +0.28% to +2.32%, 23 weeks, 7 parameters); the interval lies above zero. All-carrier fares, with the TSA traveler control: a 1% rise in fuel goes with a +1.12% change in the fare index summed over the same week and the 4 weeks after (95% interval +0.23% to +2.01%, 23 weeks, 7 parameters); the interval lies above zero. The United estimate depends on how many weeks of lagged fuel are allowed: lags 0-2: +0.38% (-0.24% to +1.00%, 18 residual degrees of freedom); lags 0-6: +1.95% (+1.55% to +2.35%, 14 residual degrees of freedom). Across lag lengths 2, 4, 6, weekly averages or week-end values, with and without the traveler control, the interval includes zero in 6 of 12 United specifications. A summed response above 1% is larger than passing the extra fuel cost through in full would produce, because fuel is only part of an airline's costs; estimates that large indicate fares and fuel moving together for other reasons, such as the summer peak. This is one episode of 23 weekly changes, built from 8,095,627 search quotes on 167 search days. It describes what happened; it does not by itself measure how fares respond to fuel.
n_quotes_note: Quote rows behind the cells of the all-carrier index, summed over search days. The source file holds 82,138,753 rows in total, 26.9% of them nonstop.
daily_note: index_* = 100 on 2022-04-17. fuel is USD per gallon and null on days without a print; an index is null on days the scrape has no usable quotes. Nothing is filled forward.

fuel_path.series: EIA Gulf Coast kerosene-type jet fuel, daily spot

any_economy.description: cheapest economy quote of either kind (basic or not), total fare including taxes and fees

basic_economy.description: cheapest basic-economy quote, total fare including taxes and fees

main_economy_base_fare.description: cheapest economy quote that is not basic economy, base fare before taxes and fees

lead_lag.definition: Pearson correlation of the weekly log change in the fare index with the weekly log change in jet fuel lag_weeks earlier. Positive lag_weeks: fuel moved first. Negative: fares moved first.
lead_lag.weekly: Weekly level = mean of daily logs over the ISO week (Monday to Sunday); a week needs at least 5 index days or 3 fuel prints. Fuel changes before and after the fare window come from the full fuel history, so every lag uses the same fare weeks.
lead_lag.interval: 95% percentile interval from a moving-block bootstrap of week pairs (blocks of 3 weeks, 2000 draws, seed 20221005). Approximate with this few weeks.

distributed_lag.definition: Weekly log change in the fare index on a constant and the weekly log change in jet fuel of the same week and each of the 4 weeks before. Coefficients are elasticities (percent per percent); `cumulative` sums them through each lag and `long_run` is the full sum. Newey-West standard errors; intervals use Student t with the residual degrees of freedom.
distributed_lag.demand_control: Weekly log change in mean daily TSA checkpoint travelers, same week (data/lab/tsa_daily.csv).

robustness.note: The summed fuel coefficient for every specification computed, none selected on its result. `not_computed` appears where a series lacks a full run of weeks.

method: Each row of the source is one itinerary Expedia offered on one search date for one flight date; we keep nonstop economy itineraries on a single carrier, searched 7 to 48 days before departure. For every search date, route, carrier and flight date we take the cheapest economy quote that is not basic economy, total fare including taxes and fees, so listing more or fewer itineraries at higher prices does not move it. These prices are grouped into cells of route x carrier x days-to-departure bucket (7-13, 14-20, 21-34, 35-48 days, each a whole number of weeks, so a cell always holds each departure weekday equally often); a cell counts on a search date when at least 85% of its departure days have a quote, and it is kept only if it counts on at least 95% of the search dates on which its bucket was scraped. From one search date to the next the index moves by the equal-weighted average log price change of the kept cells quoted that day, each measured against that same cell's own earlier price, and the changes are chained from 100 on the first search date. A cell that is not quoted on a day is carried at the average movement of the others, so a change in which routes, carriers or booking windows were scraped cannot move the index, and a cell that disappears simply stops contributing.

choices.primary_variant_description: cheapest economy quote that is not basic economy, total fare including taxes and fees
choices.price_note: Total fare (with taxes and fees) is used because base fare is not comparable across carriers. Some carriers quote base fares near zero and carry the price in fees (NK: lowest base fare $0.01, 27% of its nonstop economy quotes under $15), which makes log changes in base fare meaningless for them. Base fare is kept as a variant.

limits: These are prices quoted in Expedia searches, not tickets sold: there are no quantities, no corporate or direct-channel fares, and a quoted fare may never have been bought.

One episode: 2022-04-17 to 2022-10-05, 23 weekly changes. It spans the summer travel peak, so the seasonal rise and fall of fares overlaps the rise and fall of fuel and this window cannot separate them. Each search date prices flights 7 to 48 days ahead, so the travel dates themselves move from spring into the summer peak and on to autumn.

Routes are limited to nonstop flights among the 16 airports in the dataset (ATL, BOS, CLT, DEN, DFW, DTW, EWR, IAD, JFK, LAX, LGA, MIA, OAK, ORD, PHL, SFO); this is not United's network and has no international or connecting itineraries.

The United index rests on 120 cells on 47 routes that were quoted with a non-basic economy fare nearly every day; United has kept cells on 104 routes when basic-economy quotes are also counted. Routes where the cheapest fare shown was usually basic economy drop out of the primary index.

Fare-class mix in the scrape changed during the window: basic economy was 9% of United's nonstop economy quote rows in 2022-05 and 46% in 2022-09. The primary index excludes basic-economy quotes; the any_economy variant includes them and falls further.

No index on 5 calendar day(s) inside the window (2022-05-15, 2022-05-16, 2022-05-17, 2022-08-29, 2022-09-20): the scrape has no rows or only departures less than a week out. The scraper's horizon varies by day and 16 search day(s) have fewer than half the median number of rows; the index is chained across these gaps.

The index follows the cheapest quote in each cell; fares paid, the mix of fare classes sold and seats sold can move differently. Flight dates near holidays pass through the booking-window buckets and move the index for reasons unrelated to fuel.

With this few weeks the bootstrap and Newey-West intervals are approximate and tend to be too narrow, and 21 leads and lags were scanned, so about one interval excluding zero is expected by chance alone.
